newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam talks with Laos on electricity imports.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam talks with Laos on electricity imports.

text.p: Vietnam may import electricity from neighbouring Laos to meet fast-growing domestic demand, the state-owned power company Electricity of Vietnam (EVN) said on Thursday.

"We are thinking of the possibility of buying electricity because we have quite rapid economic growth but...difficulties building our own power stations," a senior company official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
He said the matter had been discussed at meetings between electricity officials from both countries.

However, he denied a magazine report that EVN and the Lao Committee for Electricity and Energy Programme had signed an agreement under which Laos would supply Vietnam from its southern hydroelectric plants for 25-30 years starting in 2002 or 2003.
The official said Vietnam would join a network of regional countries for cross-border supply of electricity.
At present Vietnam supplies electricity to a northern border area of Laos. But in the future, it will have to import electricity from Laos to fill a gap in its own resources.
Vietnam's rapid economic growth has brought a surge in demand for power and a growing shortfall in supply.
Power cuts in the country's towns and cities, especially in the south, are common and many rural areas still have little or no electricity at all.
EVN expects total domestic output of power this year to be 16.4 billion kilowatt hours (kwh), an increase of some 35 percent since 1994. However, even that will fall one billion kwh short of needs.

The company is aiming to double power output to between 26 and 29 billion kwh by 2000 and continue capacity building threafter to meet growing consumption needs, which a report earlier this year said could top 60 billion kwh by 2006.
EVN's deputy director general, Tran Viet Ngai, said recently that the country would possibly need to complement thermal and hydro-power resources with nuclear power within 15 years.
